fact: Baghdad's House of Wisdom was one of the largest libraries in the world, containing works from the Islamic Golden Age
source: House of Wisdom: How the Arabs Transformed Western Civilization, Jonathan Lyons (2009)

fact: The Mongol army besieging Baghdad numbered approximately 150,000 cavalry
source: Estimates vary; Persian historian Rashid al-Din and modern historians cite figures ranging from 120,000 to over 150,000. See: The Mongol Art of War, Timothy May (2007)

fact: Caliph Al-Musta'sim refused to surrender to Hulagu Khan's demands
source: The History of the World Conqueror, Ata-Malik Juvayni (13th century); also documented in modern sources

fact: Books from Baghdad's libraries were thrown into the Tigris River, reportedly turning the water black with ink
source: Widely documented in multiple medieval sources including Rashid al-Din's Jami' al-tawarikh and Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya

fact: Baghdad's walls were designed primarily for flood control rather than military siege defense
source: When Baghdad Ruled the Muslim World, Hugh Kennedy (2004). Note: Baghdad did have defensive walls, but the city's infrastructure heavily prioritized canal and flood management; this claim is a simplification.

fact: The sack of Baghdad destroyed roughly 400 years of accumulated scholarship from the Islamic Golden Age (roughly 8th–13th centuries)
source: Widely documented; the Islamic Golden Age is generally dated c. 750–1258 CE, approximately 500 years. The '400 years' figure is an approximation.
